page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes an L3 cache of 105 MB and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for deep learning and matrix operations.

This server type does not include local NVMe storage and relies entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is configured with a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. In benchmark testing, the c7i-flex.8xlarge demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2074.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 33.6 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is solid, with a Passmark CPU score of 48904.2 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance of 35034.78.

The hardware configuration and memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:2 position this instance as a cost-efficient option for compute-intensive workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage. It is highly capable for tasks such as static web serving, where it achieved a throughput of 51.12 GB/sec, as well as text processing, image processing, and moderate LLM inference tasks. The presence of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions makes it suitable for small to medium machine learning inference workloads, though the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its use for large-scale model training.
